responseSignals.feedback: Solid particles still vibrate. Water ice has an open structure; it is not a motionless solid block at particle scale.
The water particles do not grow. A liquid takes the shape of the part of the container it occupies, not necessarily the whole container.
Gas particles move rapidly in random directions and collide. They do not grow to fill the container.

accessibility.textAlternative: Which particle model explains an ice cube's shape and volume? Options: Particles vibrate about fixed positions in an open solid structure; ice has its own shape and approximately fixed volume.; Ice particles are motionless and have no space between them.. Water is poured from a cup to a bowl without spilling. What changes? Options: Its shape changes; volume stays essentially the same because close particles can move past one another.; Its particles grow and the amount of water increases to fill the bowl.. Which model describes water vapor or the gases in a classroom's air? Options: Far-apart particles move randomly and fill available space; gas has no own fixed shape or volume.; Gas particles grow larger but stay in fixed positions..
